position: end — after the verb or a noun
modifies: verbs of being and moving; nouns (*the ground underfoot*)

senses.gloss: Under your feet; on the ground you walk on.
examples: The trail was muddy and slippery *underfoot*.
Dry leaves crunched *underfoot* as we walked.

senses.gloss: In the way, so that you keep almost stepping on someone.
examples: I can't cook with the kids *underfoot* all the time.
The puppy was always *underfoot* in the kitchen.

position: end — after *throw*, *toss*, *pitch*, *serve*
form: flat — the same form as the adjective *underhand*
contrast: In American English *underhand* is mostly about throwing (British *underarm*). The sense 'sneaky, dishonest' is usually the adjective *underhanded* (*an underhanded trick*), not this adverb.

senses.gloss: With the hand kept below the shoulder, swinging up and forward.
examples: She tossed the ball *underhand* to her little brother.
If you're just learning, serve *underhand*.
He pitched *underhand* in the office softball game.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: In a secret and dishonest way.
examples: The company was accused of acting *underhandedly*.
He *underhandedly* took credit for her work.
The deal was pushed through *underhandedly*, without a public vote.

position: end — usually after a verb of speaking or looking
contrast: *understandingly* = with sympathy (с пониманием): *She nodded understandingly*. *understandably* = for reasons anyone can see (понятно, что): *She was understandably upset*.

senses.gloss: In a sympathetic way that shows you understand someone's feelings.
examples: She nodded *understandingly* when I explained why I was late.
The doctor smiled *understandingly*.
He listened *understandingly* to all my complaints.

position: mid or end — also before its word (*undeservedly forgotten*)

senses.gloss: In a way that someone or something has not earned.
examples: The film was *undeservedly* ignored at the Oscars.
I feel I was blamed *undeservedly*.
It's an *undeservedly* forgotten novel.

position: mid — after *be*, before the phrase it stresses (*undisputedly the best*)

senses.gloss: In a way that nobody argues with.
examples: She is *undisputedly* the best player on the team.
The diner is *undisputedly* the most popular place in town.
He was *undisputedly* the leader of the group.

position: before its word — usually an adjective or participle
modifies: adjectives and participles, often after a negative (*not unduly worried*)

senses.gloss: More than is necessary or reasonable.
examples: Don't be *unduly* worried about the test.
The punishment seemed *unduly* harsh.
Doctors say there is no reason to be *unduly* alarmed.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a nervous, worried or uncomfortable way.
examples: He shifted *uneasily* in his chair.
She laughed *uneasily* and changed the subject.
The two groups live side by side *uneasily*.

position: end

senses.gloss: Without showing any feelings.
examples: She described the accident calmly and *unemotionally*.
He spoke *unemotionally* about his divorce.
The judge read the verdict *unemotionally*.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unendingly patient*); also end

senses.gloss: Without ever stopping or running out.
examples: My grandmother was *unendingly* patient with us.
The debate seemed to go on *unendingly*.
I find the subject *unendingly* fascinating.

position: end

senses.gloss: Without interest or excitement.
examples: The kids agreed *unenthusiastically* to clean their rooms.
The audience clapped *unenthusiastically* at the end.
"Sure," she said *unenthusiastically*.

position: end — also before a participle (*unequally divided*)

senses.gloss: In amounts or ways that are not the same or not fair.
examples: Wealth is distributed very *unequally* in this country.
The work was divided *unequally* between the two teams.
Men and women are still paid *unequally* for the same job.

position: mid or end — before the main verb or after it
modifies: verbs of saying, denying and showing

senses.gloss: Clearly and firmly, leaving no doubt.
examples: The senator *unequivocally* denied the charges.
Let me say *unequivocally* that we will not raise taxes.
The results show *unequivocally* that the drug works.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without ever making a mistake or missing.
examples: The dog found its way home *unerringly*.
She *unerringly* picks the best dish on the menu.
His throws hit the target *unerringly*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that is morally wrong, especially in work or business.
examples: The company behaved *unethically* by hiding the risks.
Several officials acted *unethically*, though not illegally.
The data was obtained *unethically*.

position: end — also before a participle (*unevenly distributed*)

senses.gloss: Not smoothly, regularly or equally.
examples: The paint dried *unevenly*.
Heat is spread *unevenly* through the old house.
Rain falls very *unevenly* across the state.

position: end — usually after *pass*, *go*, *end*

senses.gloss: Without anything interesting or unusual happening.
examples: The flight passed *uneventfully*.
The rest of the week went by *uneventfully*.
The protest ended *uneventfully*, with no arrests.

position: mid or end — also before its word (*unexpectedly strong*)

senses.gloss: In a way that nobody expected.
examples: My grandfather died *unexpectedly* last spring.
Sales were *unexpectedly* strong this quarter.
Our cousins showed up *unexpectedly* on Sunday morning.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unfailingly polite*); also mid

senses.gloss: Always, every single time.
examples: She was *unfailingly* polite to every customer.
He *unfailingly* remembers everyone's birthday.
The hotel staff were *unfailingly* helpful.

position: end — also mid, before a participle (*unfairly blamed*)

senses.gloss: In a way that is not fair or right.
examples: I think the referee treated us *unfairly*.
She was *unfairly* blamed for the mistake.
They played *unfairly* and still lost.

position: end — also before its word (*unfashionably long*)
contrast: The set phrase is *fashionably late* (с опозданием, как принято в обществе); *unfashionably early* is a joke built on it.

senses.gloss: In a way that is not in fashion or not what people usually do.
examples: He wore his hair *unfashionably* long.
We arrived *unfashionably* early, before any other guests.
She dressed *unfashionably* and didn't care what anyone thought.

position: end
contrast: *compare unfavorably with* means 'is worse than': *The sequel compares unfavorably with the original*. The British spelling is *unfavourably*.

senses.gloss: In a negative way; so as to look worse.
examples: The new model compares *unfavorably* with the old one.
Critics reviewed the play *unfavorably*.
Most voters view the governor *unfavorably*, a new poll shows.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unforgettably beautiful*); also end

senses.gloss: In a way so strong or striking that you cannot forget it.
examples: The view from the summit was *unforgettably* beautiful.
It was an *unforgettably* bad first date.
She played the role *unforgettably*.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unforgivably rude*); also end

senses.gloss: So badly that it cannot be forgiven.
examples: He was *unforgivably* rude to my mother.
I behaved *unforgivably* last night.
The report came in *unforgivably* late.

position: end — also mid (*ungraciously refused*)

senses.gloss: In a rude, unfriendly way, without good manners.
examples: He accepted the award rather *ungraciously*.
She *ungraciously* refused to shake his hand.
The losing candidate conceded *ungraciously*.

position: end — also mid (*ungratefully complained*)

senses.gloss: Without showing thanks for what someone has done or given.
examples: He *ungratefully* complained about the gift.
She took the money *ungratefully*, without a word of thanks.
Don't behave so *ungratefully* after all they've done for you.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Willingly and generously, without resentment.
examples: She gave her time *ungrudgingly* to the shelter.
He *ungrudgingly* admitted that his rival was the better player.
The neighbors helped us *ungrudgingly* after the flood.

position: end; front with a comma as a stance adverb
modifies: verbs and participles (*unhappily married*); the whole sentence

senses.gloss: In a sad or dissatisfied way.
examples: They were *unhappily* married for twenty years.
She sighed *unhappily* and closed the laptop.

senses.gloss: Unfortunately; used to comment on a whole statement.
examples: *Unhappily*, the treatment did not work.
The plan, *unhappily*, came too late.

position: end; also front with a comma
modifies: verbs of saying; the whole sentence

senses.gloss: In a way that does not help.
examples: "No idea," he said *unhelpfully*.
*Unhelpfully*, the manual doesn't explain the error codes.
The signs were *unhelpfully* hidden behind the trees.

position: mid or end — before the main verb or after it

senses.gloss: Immediately and without any doubt.
examples: When he proposed, she *unhesitatingly* said yes.
I would *unhesitatingly* recommend him for the job.
He jumped into the river *unhesitatingly* to save the boy.

position: end

senses.gloss: Slowly and calmly, without rushing.
examples: We walked *unhurriedly* along the beach.
She ate her breakfast *unhurriedly*.
The old man crossed the room *unhurriedly*.

position: end; also before its word (*uniformly positive*)

senses.gloss: Evenly, in the same way everywhere.
examples: Spread the sauce *uniformly* over the dough.
The chairs were spaced *uniformly* across the hall.

senses.gloss: Without exception; all the same.
examples: The reviews were *uniformly* positive.
The students were *uniformly* bored by the lecture.

position: mid or end — before the main verb or after it

senses.gloss: By one side or person alone, without the agreement of others.
examples: The president acted *unilaterally*, without asking Congress.
The company *unilaterally* changed the terms of the contract.
Neither country wants to disarm *unilaterally*.

position: before its word — usually an adjective

senses.gloss: To a degree that is hard to imagine.
examples: The universe is *unimaginably* large.
Life was *unimaginably* hard for the early settlers.
The fire spread *unimaginably* fast.

position: end — also before a participle (*unimaginatively designed*)

senses.gloss: In a dull way that shows no new ideas.
examples: The new mall is *unimaginatively* designed.
The restaurant is decorated *unimaginatively*, all beige and gray.
The sequel was *unimaginatively* called "The Return."

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that cannot be understood, heard or read.
examples: He mumbled something *unintelligibly* and walked away.
The announcer spoke almost *unintelligibly* over the loudspeaker.
The note was scrawled *unintelligibly* on a napkin.

position: mid or end — also before an adjective (*unintentionally funny*)

senses.gloss: Without meaning to; by accident.
examples: I *unintentionally* deleted the whole folder.
The movie is *unintentionally* funny.
Many wildfires are started *unintentionally* by campers.

position: end

senses.gloss: Without stopping or being stopped.
examples: The machine has run *uninterruptedly* for ten years.
It rained *uninterruptedly* for three days.
I finally got to work *uninterruptedly* for a whole afternoon.

position: before its word — an adjective, participle or noun phrase

senses.gloss: In a way that belongs to only one person, place or thing; unusually or especially.
examples: She is *uniquely* qualified for this job.
The problem is not *uniquely* American.
Each snowflake is *uniquely* shaped.

position: before its word — usually a participle (*universally accepted*); also end

senses.gloss: By everyone or everywhere.
examples: The theory is now *universally* accepted.
He was *universally* admired by his colleagues.
English is not spoken *universally*, even in the U.S.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unjustifiably high*); also end

senses.gloss: In a way that has no good reason behind it.
examples: Drug prices in the U.S. are *unjustifiably* high.
She says she was fired *unjustifiably* after twenty years.
The police acted *unjustifiably* when they used force.

position: end — also mid, before a participle (*unjustly accused*)

senses.gloss: In a way that is not fair or deserved.
examples: He was *unjustly* accused of stealing.
Many workers feel they have been treated *unjustly*.
She spent ten years in prison *unjustly*.

position: end
modifies: verbs; the set phrase *take it unkindly*

senses.gloss: In a cruel or unfriendly way.
examples: Please don't speak *unkindly* about your sister.
The critics treated her first book *unkindly*.
Don't take it *unkindly*, but I'd rather be alone.

position: mid — before the main verb; also end

senses.gloss: Without knowing or realizing what you are doing.
examples: She *unknowingly* bought a stolen car.
He had *unknowingly* broken the law.
Thousands of people may have been exposed to the virus *unknowingly*.

position: end — also mid, before a participle (*unlawfully detained*)

senses.gloss: In a way that breaks the law.
examples: The officers were accused of entering the home *unlawfully*.
He was *unlawfully* detained for three days.
The workers say they were fired *unlawfully*.

position: front — with a comma; also end after a comma
modifies: the whole sentence; often *unluckily for* someone

senses.gloss: Because of bad luck; unfortunately.
examples: *Unluckily*, it rained the whole weekend.
*Unluckily* for us, the store had just closed.
He hurt his knee the day before the race, *unluckily*.

position: end

senses.gloss: Cruelly and without stopping; without mercy.
examples: The other kids teased him *unmercifully*.
The sun beat down *unmercifully* on the marchers.
She was criticized *unmercifully* in the press.

type: manner — in a way that cannot be mistaken
position: before its word — after *be* (*unmistakably hers*); also end

senses.gloss: So clearly that it cannot be confused with anything else.
examples: The voice on the phone was *unmistakably* my mother's.
His accent is *unmistakably* Southern.
Her talent showed *unmistakably* from the first scene.

position: end; also before its word (*unnaturally quiet*)
contrast: *not unnaturally* is a formal way to say 'as you would expect, naturally': *Not unnaturally, she was upset*.

senses.gloss: In a forced or strange way that does not seem normal.
examples: He smiled *unnaturally* for the camera.
The actors spoke stiffly and *unnaturally*.

senses.gloss: More than is normal or usual.
examples: The house was *unnaturally* quiet.
Her skin looked *unnaturally* pale.

position: before its word — usually an adjective; also end

senses.gloss: When it is not needed; more than is needed.
examples: The instructions are *unnecessarily* complicated.
Please don't worry *unnecessarily*.
Patients were kept in the hospital *unnecessarily*.

position: end

senses.gloss: Quietly, without attracting attention.
examples: The waiter refilled our glasses *unobtrusively*.
She slipped *unobtrusively* out of the meeting.
Cameras were placed *unobtrusively* around the store.

position: mid or end — also front with a comma
modifies: verbs, noun phrases after *be*; the whole sentence

senses.gloss: Not formally or publicly; not with official approval.
examples: *Unofficially*, the deal is already done.
He's *unofficially* in charge of the office coffee.
The results leaked *unofficially* before the announcement.

position: end; also before its word (*unpleasantly hot*)

senses.gloss: In a way that is not nice or enjoyable.
examples: The room was *unpleasantly* hot.
She was *unpleasantly* surprised by the bill.
He laughed *unpleasantly* at my mistake.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unprecedentedly high*)

senses.gloss: To a degree that has never happened before.
examples: Interest rates were *unprecedentedly* low.
The storm brought *unprecedentedly* heavy rain to the valley.
Voter turnout was *unprecedentedly* high among young people.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that nobody can predict.
examples: The weather in the mountains changes *unpredictably*.
Gas prices jumped around *unpredictably* all year.
The dog can behave *unpredictably* around strangers.

position: mid — after *be* or before the main verb; also front
modifies: the statement, or a noun phrase after *be*

senses.gloss: Certainly; beyond any doubt.
examples: She is *unquestionably* the best candidate.
This was *unquestionably* the hottest summer on record.
*Unquestionably*, the team played better in the second half.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without asking questions or having doubts; obediently.
examples: The soldiers followed orders *unquestioningly*.
Young kids accept *unquestioningly* whatever their parents say.
She trusted him *unquestioningly*.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unrealistically high*); also end

senses.gloss: In a way that does not match what is real or possible.
examples: Your expectations are *unrealistically* high.
The budget was based on *unrealistically* optimistic forecasts.
Ads often show family life *unrealistically*.

position: before its word — *unreasonably high*; also end

senses.gloss: More than is fair or sensible; too.
examples: The rent here is *unreasonably* high.
We waited an *unreasonably* long time for the results.

senses.gloss: In a way that is not fair or sensible.
examples: I think you're behaving *unreasonably*.
The landlord *unreasonably* refused to return our deposit.

position: end — also before a participle (*unrecognizably changed*)

senses.gloss: So much that someone or something can no longer be recognized.
examples: The town has changed almost *unrecognizably* since I was a kid.
His face was swollen almost *unrecognizably* after the fight.
The old song was remixed *unrecognizably*.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unrelentingly grim*); also end

senses.gloss: Without ever stopping or becoming less strong.
examples: The summer was *unrelentingly* hot.
The movie is *unrelentingly* grim.
Reporters pursued the story *unrelentingly*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that cannot be trusted or depended on.
examples: The old printer works *unreliably* at best.
Buses run *unreliably* on weekends.
Memory works *unreliably*, especially under stress.

position: end — also before its word (*unremarkably ordinary*)

senses.gloss: In an ordinary way that nobody notices.
examples: The meeting passed *unremarkably*.
From the outside, the house looked *unremarkably* ordinary.
He played *unremarkably* in his first season.

position: end — also mid (*I unreservedly apologize*)

senses.gloss: Completely, without any doubts or conditions.
examples: The company apologized *unreservedly* for the error.
I recommend this book *unreservedly*.
She supported her husband's decision *unreservedly*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that is not good enough.
examples: The story ends *unsatisfactorily*, with too many questions left open.
My complaint was handled *unsatisfactorily*.
The dispute was settled *unsatisfactorily* for both sides.

position: end — also mid (*unscrupulously raise*)

senses.gloss: Dishonestly, without caring whether something is right or fair.
examples: Some landlords *unscrupulously* raise rents after a disaster.
The company acted *unscrupulously* to win the contract.
Scammers *unscrupulously* target elderly people.

position: before its word — an adjective of weather (*unseasonably warm*)

senses.gloss: In a way that is unusual for the time of year.
examples: It's been *unseasonably* warm this December.
An *unseasonably* cold spring killed the peach crop.
Forecasters expect an *unseasonably* wet weekend.

position: end

senses.gloss: Naturally, without worrying about what other people think.
examples: The kids danced *unselfconsciously* in the street.
She laughed *unselfconsciously* at her own joke.
He talked *unselfconsciously* about his years in prison.

position: end — also mid (*unselfishly gave up*)

senses.gloss: Putting other people's needs before your own.
examples: She gave *unselfishly* of her time and money.
The team played *unselfishly*, always looking for the open man.
He *unselfishly* gave up his seat to an elderly woman.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unshakably convinced*); also end
modifies: adjectives and participles; verbs such as *believe*

senses.gloss: So firmly that nothing can change it.
examples: She was *unshakably* convinced that he was innocent.
He believed *unshakably* in his own talent.
The fans remained *unshakably* loyal to the coach.

position: before its word — usually an adjective

senses.gloss: Extremely, usually about something too bad to describe.
examples: Conditions in the camp were *unspeakably* bad.
The crime was *unspeakably* cruel.
I was *unspeakably* sad when she left.

position: end — also before *to his feet* and similar phrases

senses.gloss: In a shaky way, as if about to fall.
examples: He got *unsteadily* to his feet.
The toddler walked *unsteadily* toward her mother.
The candle flickered *unsteadily* in the draft.

position: end — also mid (*unstintingly supported*)

senses.gloss: Generously, giving a lot of time, effort or money.
examples: She gave *unstintingly* of her time.
The nurses worked *unstintingly* through the pandemic.
He *unstintingly* supported young writers.

position: end — also mid, before *tried* (*unsuccessfully tried*)

senses.gloss: Without achieving what you were trying to do.
examples: I tried *unsuccessfully* to reach her by phone.
He ran *unsuccessfully* for mayor in 2018.
Doctors worked *unsuccessfully* to save him.

position: before its word — a participle (*unsuitably dressed*); also end

senses.gloss: In a way that is not right for the situation.
examples: He showed up *unsuitably* dressed for a funeral.
The hikers were *unsuitably* equipped for the cold.
Some students were placed *unsuitably* in advanced classes.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without any idea that something bad or surprising is about to happen.
examples: He walked *unsuspectingly* into his own surprise party.
Thousands of people *unsuspectingly* clicked the link.
The tourists *unsuspectingly* handed their passports to a fake officer.

position: mid or end — also before its word (*unswervingly loyal*)

senses.gloss: Firmly and steadily, without ever changing direction.
examples: He remained *unswervingly* loyal to the president.
She has pursued her goal *unswervingly* for years.
The campaign stuck *unswervingly* to its message.

position: end
modifies: verbs of speaking, listening and showing
contrast: *sympathetic* is a false friend: it means сочувствующий, not симпатичный. So *unsympathetically* means без сочувствия, not несимпатично.

senses.gloss: Without showing kindness or understanding for someone's problems.
examples: The clerk listened *unsympathetically* to my story.
"That's your problem," he said *unsympathetically*.
The film portrays the father *unsympathetically*.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unthinkably expensive*); also front with a comma

senses.gloss: To a degree, or in a way, that is almost impossible to imagine.
examples: Housing has become *unthinkably* expensive for young families.
The losses were *unthinkably* high.
*Unthinkably*, the champions lost in the first round.

position: mid — before the main verb; also end

senses.gloss: Without thinking about what you are doing or its results.
examples: I *unthinkingly* hit Reply All.
People *unthinkingly* repeat what they read online.
She reached for the hot pan *unthinkingly*.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that is not true; falsely.
examples: He answered the question *untruthfully* under oath.
She claimed, *untruthfully*, that she had never met him.
Applicants who respond *untruthfully* can be denied a visa.

position: front — with a comma, often *untypically for* someone; also before its word (*untypically quiet*)

senses.gloss: In a way that is not usual for a person, place or thing.
examples: *Untypically* for him, he forgot her birthday.
The senator was *untypically* quiet during the debate.
The weather was *untypically* cold for May.

position: before its word — usually an adjective (*unusually warm*); also front with a comma
modifies: adjectives and adverbs; the whole sentence (*unusually for him*)

senses.gloss: More than is normal; in a way that is not usual.
examples: It's *unusually* quiet in here today.
She is an *unusually* talented musician.
*Unusually* for him, he arrived on time.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Firmly and steadily, without changing or doubting.
examples: She stood *unwaveringly* by her husband during the trial.
His eyes stared *unwaveringly* into mine.
The party has *unwaveringly* supported the policy.

position: mid or end

senses.gloss: Without wanting to; against your wishes.
examples: He *unwillingly* agreed to help.
She was dragged *unwillingly* into the argument.
The kids went to bed *unwillingly*.

position: mid or end — also front with a comma

senses.gloss: In a way that is not sensible.
examples: He *unwisely* put all his savings into one stock.
*Unwisely*, I told her the truth.
They spent the money *unwisely*.

position: mid — before the main verb

senses.gloss: Without knowing or intending it.
examples: She *unwittingly* helped the thieves by leaving the door open.
Many users *unwittingly* installed the virus.
He had *unwittingly* become part of the scam.

position: end — after a verb of motion or position

senses.gloss: Toward the place a river comes from; against the current.
examples: Salmon swim *upriver* to lay their eggs.
We paddled two miles *upriver*.
The town is about 30 miles *upriver* from New Orleans.

position: end; also before its word (*uproariously funny*)

senses.gloss: In a very loud, noisy way, especially with laughter.
examples: The audience laughed *uproariously*.
The movie is *uproariously* funny.
They celebrated *uproariously* until dawn.

ru: на север штата, в провинции штата
position: end — after a verb of motion or position
contrast: An American word: the part of a state far from its biggest city, usually to the north — above all *upstate New York*. The same form is an adjective (*an upstate town*). In crime stories *sent upstate* means 'sent to prison'.

senses.gloss: In or to the part of a state away from its main city, usually the north.
senses.ru: на север штата, в провинции штата
examples: My parents moved *upstate* after they retired.
She grew up *upstate*, near the Canadian border.
We're driving *upstate* for the weekend.

position: before its word — *mobile*
contrast: Outside *upwardly mobile* (стремящийся подняться по социальной лестнице), use *upward*: *Prices moved upward*.

senses.gloss: Toward a higher social or economic position, in *upwardly mobile*.
examples: The neighborhood attracts *upwardly* mobile young professionals.
They were an *upwardly* mobile family, the first to go to college.
The suburbs filled with *upwardly* mobile couples in the 1950s.

position: end; *upwards of* goes before a number
contrast: Americans usually say *upward*, the British *upwards*, but both appear in American writing. *upwards of 100* means 'more than 100' (свыше), not 'up to 100'.

senses.gloss: Toward a higher place or level.
examples: The smoke drifted *upwards* into the night sky.
Prices have been creeping *upwards* all year.

senses.gloss: More than a stated number, in *upwards of*.
examples: *Upwards of* 200 people showed up.
A new roof can cost *upwards of* $15,000.

position: end — after a verb of motion or position, often with *of*

senses.gloss: Against the direction the wind is blowing.
examples: The sailboat moved slowly *upwind*.
Biking *upwind* is exhausting.

senses.gloss: On the side the wind is coming from, so smells and smoke blow away from you.
examples: Stand *upwind* of the campfire so the smoke doesn't get in your eyes.
Deer can smell hunters who are *upwind* of them.

position: mid or end — also before a participle (*urgently needed*)

senses.gloss: In a way that shows something must be done right away.
examples: Blood donors are *urgently* needed.
She whispered *urgently* in my ear.
I need to talk to you *urgently*.

position: end — also mid, after a modal (*can usefully add*)

senses.gloss: In a way that helps or achieves something.
examples: You could spend your time more *usefully*.
The book can be *usefully* read alongside the textbook.
There's nothing more I can *usefully* add.

position: end

senses.gloss: In a way that does no good or has no purpose.
examples: His broken arm hung *uselessly* at his side.
The fire extinguisher sat *uselessly* in the locked closet.
I spent the afternoon searching *uselessly* for my keys.

position: end — usually after a verb of looking

senses.gloss: With an empty look, as if not thinking or not paying attention.
examples: He stared *vacantly* out the window.
She smiled *vacantly* and didn't answer.
The patient looked *vacantly* at the doctor.

position: mid or end — also before its word (*vaguely familiar*)

senses.gloss: Not clearly or exactly.
examples: I *vaguely* remember meeting him at a party.
She waved *vaguely* toward the back of the store.
He answered *vaguely* when I asked about his plans.

senses.gloss: Slightly; a little.
examples: His face looked *vaguely* familiar.
I felt *vaguely* uneasy about the whole thing.

position: mid or end
contrast: The adjective *vain* means both 'useless' and 'conceited' (тщеславный), but *vainly* nearly always means 'in vain, without success'.

senses.gloss: Without success; in vain.
examples: He searched *vainly* for his keys.
She tried *vainly* to hide her disappointment.
Rescuers worked *vainly* through the night.

position: end

senses.gloss: Bravely and with great effort, often against the odds.
examples: Firefighters fought *valiantly* to save the house.
Our team played *valiantly* but lost in overtime.
She struggled *valiantly* against the disease.

position: end — also before a participle (*validly signed*)

senses.gloss: In a way that is legally or logically correct.
examples: The contract was *validly* signed by both parties.
Only *validly* registered voters may cast a ballot.
You can't *validly* compare the two studies.
